title: Heterogeneous runtime routing and KV-cache cost model probe
content:
Purpose:

This note captures an experiment plan and early probes for integrating heterogeneous kernel backends (TensorRT, Triton, and site-specific custom kernels) with our serving runtime routing and a persistent KV cache layer. The goal is to produce actionable tradeoffs and a lightweight cost model that lets the router choose backends and caching strategies dynamically to optimize latency and per-token cost while respecting SLOs.

Background and motivation:
- We need to support multiple kernel/backends to balance cost and latency for different customers and workload shapes.
- Triton offers strong multi-model/multi-instance orchestration and easy GRPC/HTTP; TensorRT provides highest throughput for optimized kernels; custom kernels (vendor or research prototypes) can give latency wins for specific ops or sequence lengths.
- KV cache (prefix cache) can drastically reduce token compute but interacts with backend choice: cache warmup times, cache sharding, eviction, and memory fragmentation differ across runtimes.

Hypotheses:
1) A routing decision that uses a simple cost-per-token estimate + cache hit probability yields better overall spend than static routing.
2) TensorRT has lower per-token cost at high batch sizes but performs worse on cold-cache single-shot low-latency requests than Triton.
3) Persistent shared KV cache across model variants can increase hit-rate but requires careful eviction/sharding to avoid cross-tenant noisiness.

Design overview (conceptual):
- Router inputs: model_id, input_seq_len, prefix_cache_key (hash), required_latency_p99, customer_tier, recent-observed-cache-hit-rate, queue_depth.
- Router outputs: backend_choice {triton,trt,custom}, batch_strategy {single,small_batch,adaptive_batch}, kv_cache_policy {local-miss-warm, read-through, pin-on-hot}.
- Cost model: estimated_cost = (compute_token_cost / expected_batch_efficiency) * (1 - expected_cache_hit_rate) + cache_mem_amortization + backend_fixed_call_cost.
  - compute_token_cost is backend-specific and depends on quantization/profile.
  - expected_cache_hit_rate is estimated via windowed EWMA on prefix_key.

Experiment matrix (planned probes):
A) Microbench: single backend perf curves
  - Measure trt and triton across sequence lengths [8,64,256,1024], batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16], kv-cache hit/miss synthetic (full, partial, none).
  - Measure cold start/warm start latency (after model load and after K VCACHE miss path).
  - Metrics: p50,p90,p95,p99 latency; tokens/sec; GPU-util; memory-alloc; alloc-fragmentation; model-load time.

B) Router simulation: synthetic traffic replay
  - Use production trace sample (sanitized) and replay at 1x/2x/5x. Attach a simulated router that picks backends using: static (triton-only), cost-model naive (score = baseline_compute_cost*(1-hit)), and latency-aware (if required_latency_p99 < threshold choose triton).
  - Track total cost, SLO-violations, cache-hit-rate.

C) KV-cache policy probe
  - Evaluate eviction strategies LRU, size-aware-LRU, LFU, segmented-LRU for cross-tenant sharing.
  - Test pin-hot: pin top-N prefixes per tenant in GPU memory; measure effect on throughput and 95th latency.
  - Evaluate read-through vs write-through policies for warming caches behind Triton/TensorRT paths.

D) Custom-kernel edge cases
  - Run custom kernels for attention/skipping ops and measure interoperability cost when migrating requests between backends mid-session (KV cache format compatibility).
  - Evaluate small custom operator that reduces kv payload size by 20% and tradeoff in CPU pre/post processing time.

Preliminary measurements (sanity-run notes, synthetic notebook results):
- Single-GPU RTX A6000, benchmark model: 7B-ish transformer optimizer profile.
- TensorRT profile: at batch>=8 and seq<=256, tokens/sec was ~2.4x Triton FP16 baseline; p95 latency at batch 8 and seq 64 = 32ms vs Triton 58ms.
- Cold single-shot (batch=1, seq<=64): Triton had p95 18ms, TRT p95 36ms (host-to-device + kernel launch overhead).
- KV-cache warm-hit reduces per-token latency by ~60% across both; but persistent pinning increased memory pressure (non-linear fragmentation) on TRT runtime leading to occasional OOM at 92% memory.
- Read-through warming (on miss, trigger async background prefetch of future tokens) improved 95th latency on tail-heavy replay by ~15% after steady-state warmup.

Key tradeoffs observed so far:
- Throughput vs single-shot latency: TRT wins at throughput but loses at single-shot and cold-start due to static optimized kernels and longer launch overhead. Triton excels for many low-latency requests and can host many small models with less overhead.
- Cache persistence: Shared KV cache across backends reduces redundant work but requires canonicalization of cache format and versioning. Converting KV formats on the fly incurs CPU cost and may negate benefits.
- Memory management: TRT allocator behavior causes fragmentation when clients pin many small prefixes; custom allocator hooks (pooling) help but require engineering in TN runtime.
- Predictability: Triton + dynamic batching is more predictable for p99 SLAs; TRT throughput spikes can be higher variance depending on batch mixing.

Routing heuristic prototype (pseudocode):
- inputs: req {model, seq_len, latency_budget, tenant_tier, prefix_hash}
- cache_p = lookup_cache_hit_prob(prefix_hash)
- trt_score = trt_per_token_cost(seq_len)/batch_factor(seq_len) * (1 - cache_p) + trt_fixed
- triton_score = triton_per_token_cost(seq_len)/batch_factor(seq_len) * (1 - cache_p) + triton_fixed
- if latency_budget < LATENCY_THRESHOLD_SINGLE_SHOT && cache_p < CACHE_COLD_THRESHOLD: choose triton
- else choose backend with min(score) but penalize variance for lower tiers (add jitter_penalty)
Instrumentation and data needed:
- Per-prefix cache hit/miss time series sampled at 1m windows (store EWMA, hit_count, miss_count).
- Per-backend kernel launch overhead histogram.
- Memory fragmentation traces (alloc/free sizes over time) aggregated per-GPU.
- Router decision log (input features + chosen backend + reason tag) for offline analysis.

Open questions / risks:
1) Canonical KV cache representation: do we define a single wire format and force conversion at ingress (cost on CPU) or keep backend-specific formats and do on-demand conversion?
2) How to safely pin prefixes for multi-tenant workloads? Need eviction isolation and tenant memory quotas.
3) Does read-through async warming introduce cascading load when cache miss storms occur? Need rate-limiting and backoff.
4) How to quantify backend variance penalty into the cost model (we currently use mean cost, but p95 matters for SLAs).
5) Compatibility: some custom kernels require pre/post processing steps that change latency profile; how to express these in router features?

Operational considerations (rollout):
- Canary stage: run router-only-suggestion mode for 2 weeks on 5% traffic to collect logs and validate model without actually switching backends.
- Shadow mode: route 100% decisions to the router but continue to serve on baseline; compare outcomes and estimate cost delta.
- Small canary switch for low-tier tenants with lenient SLAs.

Next steps and action items (owners and ETA):
- A1: Finish full microbench across seq lengths and quantization profiles (owner: Diego Alvarez) ETA 2025-03-18.
- A2: Implement router decision logging and minimal cost-model scoring code in runtime (owner: Jonah Reed) ETA 2025-03-10.
- A3: Run replay simulation with sampled production trace and baseline vs cost-model routing (owner: Maya Patel) ETA 2025-03-22.
- A4: Prototype canonical KV cache wire format and a conversion shim for TRT/Triton (owner: Priya Singh) ETA 2025-03-28.
- A5: Draft an SRE runbook for memory fragmentation mitigation (owner: eng-sre, contact: Jonah Reed) ETA 2025-03-12.
Notes to self:
- Keep experiment artifacts (notebook, flamegraphs, kernel logs) attached to JIRA-IR-512.
- Slack thread: #runtime-kernel-integration has ongoing commentary — reference messages around Feb 2025 for allocator patches.

Appendix: quick cost-model example calculation (toy numbers)
- TRT per-token compute cost: $0.0007 at batch 8, Triton: $0.0012 at batch 1.
- Expected cache hit rate (EWMA) = 0.35.
- TRT estimated = 0.0007*(1-0.35)+0.0001 (fixed) = 0.000555
- Triton estimated = 0.0012*(1-0.35)+0.00005 = 0.00083
- Router picks TRT when throughput can be batched; but if latency_budget < 50ms and cache_p < 0.2, prefer Triton.

End of draft.

If you want, I can convert the experiment matrix into a runnable notebook skeleton and a Linear ticket list for the action items.
